facts.statement: Xilousuchus lived during the Lower Triassic (Olenekian stage) in northeastern Shanxi Province, China.
facts.quote: Xilousuchus is an extinct genus of poposauroid from lower Triassic (Olenekian stage) deposits of Fugu County of northeastern Shanxi Province, China.

facts.statement: The fossils of Xilousuchus were found in the Heshanggou Formation of the Ordos Basin.
facts.quote: It was found from the Heshanggou Formation of the Ordos Basin, Hazhen commune.

facts.statement: Xilousuchus was first described by Xiao-Chun Wu in 1981, with the type species named Xilousuchus sapingensis.
facts.quote: It was first named by Xiao-Chun Wu in 1981 and the type species is Xilousuchus sapingensis.

facts.statement: Research by Sterling J. Nesbitt in 2011 classified Xilousuchus as a poposauroid most closely related to Arizonasaurus.
facts.quote: Sterling J. Nesbitt (2011) found Xilousuchus to be a poposauroid which is most closely related to Arizonasaurus.

facts.statement: Xilousuchus is currently considered the oldest known archosaur, though it may be slightly younger than Ctenosauriscus and Vytshegdosuchus by less than one million years.
facts.quote: Xilousuchus is the oldest archosaur to date, although Ctenosauriscus and Vytshegdosuchus might be even older by less than one million years.

facts.statement: Xilousuchus was likely a large animal, estimated to be between three and four meters in length.
facts.quote: Xilousuchus was probably quite a large animal when alive, possibly between three and four metres long.

facts.statement: Xilousuchus possessed a small head and a sail-like structure running along its neck and back.
facts.quote: It had a small head, and a sail along its neck and back.

facts.statement: The preserved skull of Xilousuchus is fragmentary but includes much of the snout and maxilla.
facts.quote: The skull is fragmentary, but much of the snout and maxilla are present.

facts.statement: The single preserved maxillary tooth was nearly 15 mm long, and the presence of replacement teeth indicates that Xilousuchus was a polyphyodont.
facts.quote: The single preserved maxillary tooth is large, almost 15 mm long, and in other dental alveoli where the teeth are missing replacement teeth are sometimes visible, indicating that it was a polyphyodont.

facts.statement: The teeth of Xilousuchus had small serrations and were curved backwards, suggesting they could puncture flesh or slice chunks of food.
facts.quote: The tooth has small serrations, is curved backwards, and is laterally compressed, indicating that it could have punctured flesh or possibly sliced off chunks.

facts.statement: Large, flattened neural spines on the cervical vertebrae formed a sail-like structure along the neck, similar to other ctenosauriscids.
facts.quote: The cervical vertebrae have large, flattened neural spines which make up most of their height and would have formed a sail-like structure in life, similar to other ctenosauriscids.

facts.statement: The neural spines on the neck vertebrae increased in height from 42 mm at the axis vertebra to 92 mm at the tenth cervical vertebra.
facts.quote: The spines gradually increase in height as they move backwards - that on the axis vertebra is 42 mm high, whereas that on the tenth cervical vertebra is 92 mm high.

facts.statement: Xilousuchus likely had long, powerful legs and was probably an active hunter.
facts.quote: It probably had long and quite powerful legs, and would have been an active hunter.

facts.statement: Xilousuchus belongs to the family Ctenosauriscidae.
